races.name: Virgin Bet Daily Price Boosts "National Hunt" Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Loriko
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with class advantage but disappointing recent form, 31 days off and needs to bounce back from below-par efforts
runners_data.comment: Showed some fairly useful form in the autumn but comes here with a point to prove
runners_data.spotlight: Showed some fairly useful form last autumn but his handicap debut in December was disappointing and he was again below par when a short-odds second in Plumpton maiden (2m, good) last month; should be fine over this longer trip but has a point to prove.

runners_data.name: Katarcice
runners_data.note: Course winner over shorter trip with fresher profile, only two rules starts but showed promise on hurdle debut here
runners_data.comment: Second over 2m here on last month's hurdling debut and this longer trip ought to suit
runners_data.spotlight: Placed in two Irish points last spring and on both rules starts in March and April, latterly when second here (2m, good) on hurdle debut; ought to be suited by this longer trip and has less to prove than his rival.

races.paceDynamic: With only two runners, this becomes a tactical match between two hold-up horses who both prefer to race from off the pace. Neither Loriko nor Katarcice has natural pace-setting instincts, creating an unusual dynamic where someone must reluctantly lead. The absence of genuine front-runners means whoever goes forward will likely dictate a moderate tempo throughout the 2m4½f journey. This scenario strongly favours the horse with superior acceleration and finishing kick, as the restrained early pace will set up a sprint finish between two relatively fresh horses.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Reluctant Leader Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Loriko takes up the running early and dictates terms
scenarios.body: The higher-rated horse can control the tempo to suit his finishing kick and prove too strong in the straight. His superior class rating (OR 121 vs 114) becomes decisive when both horses arrive relatively fresh at the business end.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Patient Tracker Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If Katarcice forces Loriko to lead and tracks him patiently
scenarios.body: The less experienced horse can use his recent course form advantage and fresher profile to outfinish the favourite. His second place here over 2m on good ground in April gives him a tactical edge at this venue.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Slow Early Kick
scenarios.trigger: If both horses refuse to lead early creating a crawling pace
scenarios.body: The race becomes a pure test of acceleration from the final hurdle, where Loriko's higher TopSpeed rating (117 vs 96) proves decisive. The lack of early pace exaggerates the importance of raw finishing speed over stamina.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Early Duel Backfires
scenarios.trigger: If both horses are pushed along from early to establish position
scenarios.body: The unexpectedly strong early pace compromises both finishers, creating a war of attrition that neither truly wants. Katarcice's lighter recent racing schedule gives him a marginal fitness advantage in a slog.

watchPoints.text: Watch the early pace - if both horses are reluctant to lead it could create an unusually slow tempo that turns this into a sprint
Monitor Loriko's jumping rhythm early as his confidence needs rebuilding after recent disappointing efforts
If Katarcice gets first run in the straight his course advantage could prove decisive despite the class differential

races.name: Virgin Bet Daily Extra Places Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Koapey
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with promising chase debut form but three non-completions since October win, returns after 26 days off
runners_data.comment: Three non-completions have followed his promising chase debut; can still get back on track
runners_data.spotlight: Low-mileage 6yo; three non-completions have followed last October's promising chase/handicap debut but he was running fairly well before penultimate-fence fall in 2m Chepstow race won by Pep Talking last month; moves up in trip with Sean Bowen enlisted here; still has plenty of time to get career back on track.

runners_data.name: William Cody
runners_data.note: Course specialist with three C&D wins, ran well in final two starts last season over similar distances, 51 days since last run
runners_data.comment: Three-time C&D winner; returns here after going close on last two outings; obvious claims
runners_data.spotlight: Gained three of four chase wins over C&D and returns here after going close on final two starts last season (2m4f/2m3f; wore cheekpieces last time); holds no secrets from the handicapper but will be fine on the forecast good ground and has obvious claims.

runners_data.name: Big Boy Barney
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who won comfortably at C&D in March, wears tongue-tie and comes from inform Fergal O'Brien yard
runners_data.comment: Won very comfortably over C&D in March and again ran well at Southwell last month
runners_data.spotlight: Off the mark over fences at second attempt, with very comfortable win in four-runner C&D (good) contest in March; again ran well when third at Southwell (2m4f, good; albeit finished tired) last month and is sure to be suited by the return to this track.

runners_data.name: Hurricane Bay
runners_data.note: Front-runner who needs cheekpieces to show his best, has been below form recently despite good handicap mark
runners_data.comment: Ran well for a long way over 3m last time but has been well below his best for a while now
runners_data.spotlight: Well handicapped if judged on his two good-ground wins in cheekpieces last spring (2m7f/2m5f) but has been well below best (in various headgear) in recent months; ran well for a long way before weakening quickly at Market Rasen (3m, good) last time and might benefit from this drop back in trip but others have much less to prove.

runners_data.name: Ice In The Veins
runners_data.note: Chase debutant who raced too freely in hurdle finale, hold-up style under Harry Skelton from good mark
runners_data.comment: 2-7 over hurdles last season; makes chasing debut from a good mark; interesting
runners_data.spotlight: 2-7 over hurdles last season; raced too freely and disappointed when favourite for a valuable series final last month but makes chasing debut from a good mark; big player if he gets into a good jumping rhythm.

runners_data.name: Pep Talking
runners_data.note: In-form front-runner coming off 10-length Chepstow win, wears prism cheekpieces and has excellent 7-17 chase record
runners_data.comment: Career-best form when winning by 10l at Chepstow last month; now 7-17 over fences
runners_data.spotlight: Took form to another new level when winning by 10l from the front at Chepstow (2m, good to soft) last month and is now 7-17 over fences (includes course win); today's trip-and-ground combination will also suit; respected.

races.paceDynamic: Hurricane Bay and Pep Talking are both confirmed front-runners who will contest the early lead, creating an honest gallop from the start. Pep Talking comes off a dominant 10-length front-running win at Chepstow and will want to dictate, while Hurricane Bay has shown his best form leading in cheekpieces. With two keen pace-setters and a small field, the gallop will be solid throughout but not breakneck pace. This race shape favours the prominent racers like Koapey and William Cody who can track the leaders without getting involved in the early battle, then strike when the front-runners tire.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the two leaders Hurricane Bay and Pep Talking engage in a pace duel from the start
scenarios.body: The sustained gallop will suit horses like William Cody and Koapey who can sit just behind and pounce when the leaders weaken. William Cody has three C&D wins and ran well in his last two starts, while Koapey showed promise before recent falls.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Pep Talking gets an uncontested lead while Hurricane Bay struggles early
scenarios.body: Pep Talking can dictate at his own pace and repeat his dominant Chepstow performance from the front. His recent 10-length win and 7-17 chase record shows he can control races when allowed to lead freely.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuine and the leaders come back significantly in the final furlong
scenarios.body: Big Boy Barney's hold-up style could prove effective if he gets the right setup from his C&D win. Ice In The Veins making his chase debut might also benefit from a strong pace to aim at.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Early
scenarios.trigger: If both Hurricane Bay and Pep Talking fail to establish a rhythm or make errors
scenarios.body: The race could become a tactical affair where any runner with tactical speed could capitalize. This scenario would likely favor the more experienced chasers who can adapt to a messy pace.

watchPoints.text: Hurricane Bay could set unsustainable fractions if he tries to match Pep Talking's early pace given his recent poor form
Ice In The Veins showed free-running tendencies in his last hurdle start which could be problematic on chase debut
Koapey's jumping after three recent falls including a penultimate fence tumble when going well
William Cody's fitness after 51-day break despite strong course record
Big Boy Barney needs the front-runners to go a strong pace to set up his hold-up style in this small field

races.name: Virgin Bet A Good Bet Mares' Handicap Chase (Queen Boudicca Mares' Chase Series Qualifier) (GBB)

runners_data.name: Another Day Out
runners_data.note: Strong stayer returning to chasing after recent hurdle win, 50 days off suitable for seasoned front-runner
runners_data.comment: Battled well for course hurdle win in March and returns to chasing on a good mark
runners_data.spotlight: Three-time chase winner (once over C&D); lost her way over fences during the winter but battled well for narrow hurdle win here (3m1f, good; front pair well clear) in March and reverts to this code on a good mark.

runners_data.name: Catwalk Girl
runners_data.note: Inexperienced amateur-ridden leader facing step up in class, recent fall shows jumping remains question mark
runners_data.comment: Point winner; fell mid-race on recent handicap hurdle debut; still unexposed under rules
runners_data.spotlight: Won small-field maiden point last spring and showed some promise in maiden/novice hurdles this year; fell mid-race on recent handicap hurdle debut but remains unexposed under rules and Max Comley is evidently keen to switch her to chasing.

runners_data.name: Lady Jago
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare struggling since stable switch, needs pace collapse to be effective from rear
runners_data.comment: Generally disappointing for current stable but now too well handicapped to rule out
runners_data.spotlight: Three-time chase winner (2m4f-3m1f) on good ground for Dan Skelton in spring 2025; generally very disappointing for current stable since the autumn, including when back on a sound surface for last two starts, but has become too well handicapped to rule out.

runners_data.name: Kit's Coty
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with best recent form and Ludlow win over Another Day Out provides confidence
runners_data.comment: Rather disappointing since October's Ludlow win but might be boosted by cheepieces
runners_data.spotlight: 1-10 over fences, the win gained on last season's reappearance at Ludlow (3m, good; Another Day Out second) in October; not in same form again since but now 2lb below that mark, and might be boosted by new cheekpieces.

races.paceDynamic: Catwalk Girl and Another Day Out are both confirmed front-runners who will contest the early lead, creating an honest gallop from the outset with no restraint likely from either. Kit's Coty will sit prominently behind this pace, while Lady Jago as the sole hold-up horse will track from the rear in this small field. The dual pace angle up front should create a strong tempo over this stamina-testing trip, setting up the race for those who can sustain their effort rather than rely on a finishing kick. This honest pace scenario strongly favours prominent runners and front-runners with stamina, as Lady Jago's hold-up style will struggle to make up ground against horses who have been closer to a solid tempo throughout.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front Runners Duel Hard
scenarios.trigger: If Catwalk Girl and Another Day Out go at it hammer and tongs from flag-fall
scenarios.body: The pace becomes very strong early with both leaders committed, creating maximum stamina test that plays to Another Day Out's proven staying power. Kit's Coty picks up the pieces late as the early leaders tire, while Lady Jago finds too much to do from the back.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Controlled Front Running
scenarios.trigger: If one of the leaders (likely Another Day Out) gets an easy lead with Catwalk Girl settling
scenarios.body: The pace becomes more measured allowing the leader to control fractions and kick clear, with inexperienced Catwalk Girl unable to match the acceleration. Lady Jago gets into contention but the winner has already flown.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Prominent Challenge
scenarios.trigger: If Kit's Coty travels sweetly behind the pace and both leaders go too hard early
scenarios.body: The early gallop takes its toll on Catwalk Girl and Another Day Out, allowing Kit's Coty to strike late with her class advantage. Her Ludlow win over Another Day Out gives confidence she can repeat the dose.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Success
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is surprisingly moderate and Lady Jago gets the race run to suit
scenarios.body: The tempo lacks bite allowing Lady Jago to stay closer than usual and her three chase wins suggest she has the class when conditions align. Her hold-up style works when the pace collapses.

watchPoints.text: Another Day Out's jumping under pressure if Catwalk Girl forces a strong early pace
Catwalk Girl's inexperience with amateur pilot Mr James King when racing gets serious
Lady Jago's ability to get competitive from hold-up position given poor recent efforts
Kit's Coty's fitness after 38-day break having shown best form fresh last season

races.name: Virgin Bet Mares' Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Mermaids Cave
runners_data.note: Hold-up style faces difficult task with likely controlled pace, wearing cheekpieces again after moderate recent efforts
runners_data.comment: Not beaten far when fifth at Fakenham last month and continues to slip down the weights
runners_data.spotlight: 7-27 over hurdles, including a good-ground C&D win; not firing on all cylinders since last autumn but wasn't beaten far when fifth of seven in refitted cheekpieces at Fakenham (2m4f, good) last month and continues to slip down the weights.

runners_data.name: Mary
runners_data.note: Front-runner should dictate terms unchallenged early, good recent Warwick win suggests she's back in form at this trip
runners_data.comment: Won from the front in September and returned from break with encouraging run last month
runners_data.spotlight: Returned to form with front-running win at Warwick (2m3f, good) in September and caught the eye at Stratford (2m, good) last month, after a break, making good headway from a long way off the pace before fading into fifth on the run-in; back up in trip here and it will be interesting to see whether she reverts to much more positive tactics.

runners_data.name: Notnowlinda
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse needing strong pace to be effective, cheekpieces helped at Uttoxeter but still below peak form
runners_data.comment: Ran well when third in first-time cheekpieces in March and good ground will suit
runners_data.spotlight: Yet to match peak form since returning from long absence in the autumn but her third in first-time cheekpieces at Uttoxeter (2m4f, good to soft) in late March was a pretty good effort, and she'll be fine on the forecast good ground here.

runners_data.name: No No Fizz
runners_data.note: Prominent style suits race shape perfectly, course winner in March but trainer blamed ground for poor Uttoxeter run
runners_data.comment: Back in good nick when scoring over C&D in March but pulled up since; hard to predict
runners_data.spotlight: Looked back in good nick when scoring over C&D (good) in March but ran poorly and was pulled up at Uttoxeter last month (trainer blamed the good to soft ground); has become hard to predict.

runners_data.name: Hope Rising
runners_data.note: Promising prominent runner returning from 208-day break, three good-ground wins suggest conditions ideal if fit enough
runners_data.comment: Three wins in early part of last season; off since refusing to race in October; new trip
runners_data.spotlight: Progressive over hurdles in early part of last season, winning three times on good ground (2m-2m1f); absent since blotting copybook in the autumn (whipped round at start and refused to race) and not bred to benefit from this step up in trip.

races.paceDynamic: Mary will take the field along as the sole confirmed front-runner, with No No Fizz and Hope Rising likely tracking her in prominent positions early. The presence of three hold-up horses (Mermaids Cave, Notnowlinda) and only one natural leader suggests Mary can dictate terms without serious early pressure. With good ground conditions and a moderate 2m3½f distance, this setup creates a controlled tempo that builds gradually, allowing horses to stay in contention longer. This race shape strongly favours the prominent runners who can sit close to Mary and kick from a good position, as the hold-up horses may struggle to make up ground against the likely solid pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Front-Running Display
scenarios.trigger: If Mary gets away with soft fractions early and builds a decisive lead
scenarios.body: She can use her recent Warwick form to control from the front while the hold-up brigade struggle to close the gap. The prominent duo of No No Fizz and Hope Rising would be best placed to chase but may lack the finishing kick needed.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Mary sets reasonable fractions but gets caught close home
scenarios.body: No No Fizz or Hope Rising can use their tactical speed to sit handy and pounce when Mary's stamina wanes in the final furlong. The good ground suits both their profiles perfectly for this distance.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Charges Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes genuinely strong and the field gets strung out
scenarios.body: Mermaids Cave or Notnowlinda could benefit from a truly-run race that sets up for their late finishing style. However, they need significant help from the pace scenario to be effective.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Complete Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If Mary goes too slow and the race becomes a sprint finish
scenarios.body: The tactical speed of the prominent runners becomes crucial in a bunched finish where positioning matters most. Hope Rising's class could tell in a messy finale despite the long absence.

watchPoints.text: Hope Rising's fitness after 208 days off - any market confidence would be significant given the long layoff
Mary's jumping rhythm early - needs to settle into a smooth rhythm to utilize her front-running advantage effectively
Notnowlinda and Mermaids Cave positioning turning in - both need to be within striking distance to have any chance
No No Fizz's attitude after being pulled up last time - needs to bounce back to her March course winning form
The pace through the first mile - if Mary goes too fast early it opens up the race for the hold-up horses

races.name: Virgin Bet Supports Safe Gambling Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Moviddy
runners_data.note: Front-runner returning to hurdles after disappointing fence efforts, 24 days off should have him fresh for leading role
runners_data.comment: Placed in valuable chase in January but otherwise disappointing last season; back hurdling
runners_data.spotlight: Placed in valuable series final over fences at Fakenham (2m5f, good to soft) in January but rest of last season's form was disappointing and it's hard to predict whether she'll be in the right mood for this return to hurdling; tried blinkers when pulled up last time; usual cheekpieces return.

runners_data.name: Roe And Co
runners_data.note: NON-RUNNER - would have been key pace angle with three consecutive chase wins before recent problems
runners_data.comment: Won three chases in late 2025 but out of sorts on both starts this year; now back hurdling
runners_data.spotlight: Won three consecutive chases (2m6f-3m) towards end of 2025 but looked out of sorts when pulled up on both appearances this year (bled on first occasion); reverts to hurdling and swaps cheekpieces for first-time blinkers; needs to turn things around.

runners_data.name: Indian Sunbird
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer returning after 186-day break, dual C&D winner last year suits the expected strong pace
runners_data.comment: Two wins in 2025, the latter over C&D; returns from break on fairly tough mark, though
runners_data.spotlight: Dual hurdle winner last year, latterly over C&D (good) in October; absent since lesser effort here in November, though, and will need to resume in prime form to have a chance off his current mark.

runners_data.name: Raby Mere
runners_data.note: Prominent runner back in form for new trainer, cheekpieces refitted and 3-mile trip ideal for his style
runners_data.comment: Back on song in refitted cheekpieces towards end of last season; probably in the mix
runners_data.spotlight: Back on song in refitted cheekpieces at Southwell (3m, good) in March, his third start for Caroline Fryer, and the form of his respectable fourth at Fakenham (2m7f, good) last month was well advertised by the winner there on Monday; not yet fully exposed as a stayer; probably won't be far away.

runners_data.name: Greedy Smith
runners_data.note: Prominent type with limited form on good going, needs pace collapse to be competitive at this level

runners_data.name: Braganza Bay
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist and dual C&D winner, disappointing since return but capable of big bounce back
runners_data.comment: Dual C&D winner; not at best since returning from one-year break in November; on good mark
runners_data.spotlight: Dual C&D winner; not at best since returning from one-year absence in November and was particularly disappointing when pulled up over fences last month; needs a revival but is back hurdling on a tempting mark.

races.paceDynamic: Moviddy and the returning Roe And Co are both confirmed front-runners who will contest the early lead in this small field, creating an honest gallop over the extended trip. With two genuine pace-setters likely to engage early, the tempo should be sustained rather than stop-start, though the 3m1f distance may force them to moderate slightly mid-race. The hold-up horses Indian Sunbird and Braganza Bay will benefit most from this setup, as the pace-setters are likely to soften each other up over the final mile, creating opportunities for strong finishers to sweep past tired leaders.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Prevail
scenarios.trigger: If both front-runners engage early and maintain honest pace throughout
scenarios.body: The sustained gallop plays perfectly into the hands of Indian Sunbird and Braganza Bay who can pick off tiring leaders. Strong finishers get ideal setup with pace to aim at over final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Mid-Race
scenarios.trigger: If Moviddy and Roe And Co go too fast early then significantly slow the tempo
scenarios.body: The race becomes tactical in the middle stages, suiting the prominent runners who can position closer. Raby Mere and Greedy Smith benefit from the moderate finish that develops.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Survives
scenarios.trigger: If one pace-setter gets easy lead while the other struggles or doesn't engage
scenarios.body: Moviddy or returning Roe And Co controls the race from the front without pressure. The lack of pace pressure allows the leader to save energy for sustained finish.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Crawl Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If both front-runners show early caution due to the extended distance
scenarios.body: Race becomes very slowly run affair with sprint finish over final three furlongs. This neutralizes stamina advantages and favors horses with most natural speed regardless of style.

watchPoints.text: Roe And Co withdrawal removes key pace element, making Moviddy potentially unopposed early
Indian Sunbird returning from 186-day absence needs to show immediate sharpness to capitalize on race shape
Raby Mere wearing cheekpieces again after successful return to form suggests connections expect improved effort
Braganza Bay pulled up last time over fences and needs to prove recent troubles are behind him
Weather conditions remain good across all races, confirming genuine good going for stamina test

races.name: Virgin Bet Open Maiden National Hunt Flat Race (Category 3 Elimination) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: St Julie
runners_data.comment: Half-sister to St Irene, who won a Listed mares' hurdle for connections last season
runners_data.spotlight: Seventh foal; half-sister to St Irene, who won a Listed mares' hurdle for connections last season, and a point winner; dam fair 2m1f/2m6f hurdle winner; one of two newcomers representing the stable.

runners_data.name: St Zoe
runners_data.comment: Third foal from unraced half-sister to two useful jumpers; may be stable's second string
runners_data.spotlight: 34,000euros foal; third foal; half-sister to a point winner; dam unraced half-sister to useful jumpers Carrigmartin and City Slicker; riding arrangements suggest St Julie may be the stable's main hope.

runners_data.name: Meli Melo d'Angos
runners_data.comment: Dropped out rather tamely and was beaten about 24l when eighth at Hereford last month
runners_data.spotlight: First foal from a French 2m4f/2m5f chase winner; ran well to a point but dropped out rather tamely and was beaten about 24l when eighth of 11 at Hereford (good) last month; needs that run to have brought him on.
